name: Drip-line nuclei set the r-process path
summary: The r-process runs through very neutron-rich nuclei near the neutron drip line. Their masses (neutron separation energies), shell evolution and half-lives, measured at FRIB, RIBF and FAIR, therefore fix the path and the abundance pattern. In (n,γ)⇄(γ,n) equilibrium, the waiting-point nuclei sit at S_n ≈ 2–3 MeV.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

Tanihata et al. (1985). "Measurements of Interaction Cross Sections and Nuclear Radii in the Light p-Shell Region". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 55, 2676. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2676](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2676)

name: Fission barriers bound the superheavy landscape
summary: The liquid-drop fissility rises with Z²/A, and the macroscopic fission barrier vanishes near Z≈100. Superheavy nuclei survive only because shell-correction barriers of a few MeV hold them together, and spontaneous fission competes with α decay as the terminating decay mode.
map: x=\frac{E_C}{2E_S}\approx\frac{Z^2/A}{(Z^2/A)_{\rm crit}},\ (Z^2/A)_{\rm crit}\approx50;\ B_f\approx B_f^{\rm LD}(x)+\delta E_{\rm shell}
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Oganessian et al. (2010). "Synthesis of a New Element with Atomic Number Z=117". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 104, 142502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502)

name: Alpha-decay chains identify superheavy elements
summary: New superheavy elements are identified by correlated α-decay chains that end at known nuclides. Geiger–Nuttall (Gamow tunnelling) systematics turn measured Q_α into half-lives, and kinks in Q_α along the chains reveal shell gaps on the way to the island of stability.
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
Oganessian et al. (2010). "Synthesis of a New Element with Atomic Number Z=117". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 104, 142502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502)

name: Neutron-star cores probe cold dense QCD
summary: Lattice QCD cannot reach the low-temperature, high-μ_B corner of the QCD phase diagram (quark-matter cores, color superconductivity, quarkyonic matter) because of the sign problem, and heavy-ion collisions cannot reach it either. Neutron-star masses, radii and tidal deformabilities are the only data there, and a sound speed rising above the conformal value is the sought signature.
sources: Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

name: Fission physics sets reactor criticality
summary: Each fission releases about 200 MeV and about 2.4 prompt neutrons. Reactor multiplication is built from fission and absorption cross sections and ν̄. Pairing energy lets odd-N ²³⁵U fission with thermal neutrons, while ²³⁸U needs fast neutrons above a threshold.
sources: Meitner & Frisch (1939). "Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction". *Nature* 143, 239. [doi:10.1038/143239a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/143239a0)
Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

name: Reaction theory feeds evaluated cross-section libraries
summary: Evaluated libraries (ENDF/B, JEFF, JENDL) combine measurements with reaction theory, each with covariances: R-matrix and Breit–Wigner fits in the resolved-resonance region, and Hauser–Feshbach compound-nucleus and optical-model calculations elsewhere. The same activation cross sections set isotope-production yields.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

name: Chiral-EFT neutron matter anchors the neutron-star EOS
summary: Chiral NN+3N forces, solved with quantum Monte Carlo, many-body perturbation theory or coupled cluster, give the pure-neutron-matter energy with quantified truncation errors up to about 1–2 n_0. This fixes the symmetry energy S_0 and its slope L and predicts R_1.4 ≈ 11–13 km. Three-nucleon forces dominate the uncertainty, and above about 2 n_0 the EOS is extrapolated.
breaks: Chiral EFT breaks down as momenta approach the breakdown scale (~500–600 MeV), so above ~2n_0 it gives no control.
sources: Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)
Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

name: Magic neutron numbers make the r-process peaks
summary: At the closed shells N=50, 82 and 126, neutron separation energies drop just past the closure and β half-lives at the waiting points are long. Matter therefore piles up at A≈80, 130 and 195, the r-process peaks, about 10 mass units below the s-process peaks at the same N. Whether the N=82 and N=126 gaps are quenched far from stability is still debated.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)
Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Fission recycling terminates the r-process
summary: In very neutron-rich merger ejecta the r-process reaches A≈250–300, where neutron-induced, β-delayed and spontaneous fission end the flow. The fragments recycle into A≈110–170 and shape the second peak and the rare-earth region. Fission barriers and yields of unmeasured neutron-rich actinides are among the largest nuclear uncertainties.
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

name: Gamow-peak fusion rates power stellar burning
summary: Stellar burning rates are Coulomb-barrier tunnelling probabilities folded with a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution, which gives the Gamow peak. Astrophysical S-factors for the pp chain, CNO cycle, triple-α and ¹²C(α,γ)¹⁶O are measured underground (LUNA) or extrapolated to stellar energies.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)

name: Neutron lifetime sets primordial helium
summary: The weak n↔p rates freeze out near T≈0.8 MeV at n/p≈1/6. Free-neutron decay then lowers n/p to about 1/7 before the deuterium bottleneck breaks (T≈0.07 MeV), which gives Y_p≈0.25. τ_n normalizes all the weak rates, so the ~9 s beam–bottle lifetime discrepancy feeds directly into the predicted Y_p.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Beta-decay half-lives set the r-process clock
summary: β-decay half-lives at the waiting points, often with large first-forbidden contributions, set how fast the flow climbs in Z and shape the abundance peaks. β-delayed neutron emission during freeze-out smooths and shifts the final pattern.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Beta equilibrium and Urca cooling in neutron stars
summary: Neutron-star matter sits in β equilibrium (μ_n = μ_p + μ_e), which together with the symmetry energy fixes the proton fraction. Above x_p ≈ 11–15%, direct Urca (n→p e ν̄, e p→n ν) becomes kinematically allowed and cools the star fast; below it only the slower modified Urca process operates.

name: Gamow–Teller quenching from two-body currents
summary: Shell-model Gamow–Teller rates have long needed g_A quenched to about 0.75 of its free value. Ab initio calculations with chiral two-body weak currents and many-body correlations reproduce the measured rates without ad hoc quenching. The same framework supplies the nuclear matrix elements for neutrinoless double-beta decay.

name: Liquid drop plus shell correction: fission barriers
summary: The fission barrier is the deformation energy of a liquid drop (surface against Coulomb) plus a Strutinsky shell correction from single-particle levels in the deformed well. Together they give double-humped barriers, fission isomers, and asymmetric mass splits driven by fragments near doubly magic ¹³²Sn.
map: E(\beta)=E_{\rm LD}(\beta)+\delta E_{\rm shell}(\beta)+\delta E_{\rm pair}(\beta)
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)

name: Fusion–evaporation reactions make superheavy elements
summary: Superheavy elements are made by cold fusion (Pb/Bi targets) or hot fusion (⁴⁸Ca beams on actinide targets). Cross sections of picobarns to femtobarns are the product of capture over the Coulomb barrier, competition from quasifission, and survival against fission while neutrons evaporate from the compound nucleus. Going beyond Z=118 requires ⁵⁰Ti or ⁵⁴Cr beams.
sources: Oganessian et al. (2010). "Synthesis of a New Element with Atomic Number Z=117". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 104, 142502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.142502)

name: Inverse-kinematics reactions reveal halos and shells
summary: Short-lived nuclei are studied as radioactive beams on light targets. Interaction cross sections revealed the ¹¹Li halo, knockout momentum distributions give the orbital ℓ and spectroscopic factors, and transfer and Coulomb breakup map shell evolution near the drip lines.
sources: Tanihata et al. (1985). "Measurements of Interaction Cross Sections and Nuclear Radii in the Light p-Shell Region". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 55, 2676. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2676](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2676)

name: Neutron-rich nuclei form the neutron-star crust
summary: The outer crust is a Coulomb lattice of nuclei that become more neutron-rich with depth, from ⁵⁶Fe through N=50 nuclei near ⁷⁸Ni–⁸²Zn to N=82 isotones. Its composition follows from measured and extrapolated masses. The inner crust starts at neutron drip, where S_n→0.
sources: Wang et al. (2021). "The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references". *Chinese Phys. C* 45, 030003. [doi:10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf](https://doi.org/10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf)

name: Mass and decay evaluations drive nucleosynthesis networks
summary: AME masses, NUBASE/ENSDF half-lives, and Maxwellian-averaged (n,γ) cross sections at kT≈30 keV from evaluated libraries feed the s- and r-process reaction networks. Sensitivity studies rank unmeasured masses and half-lives by their effect on abundances, and that ranking steers measurements at radioactive-beam facilities.
sources: Wang et al. (2021). "The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references". *Chinese Phys. C* 45, 030003. [doi:10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf](https://doi.org/10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf)

Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

name: Fission-product beta decay: delayed neutrons, decay heat
summary: About 0.65% of ²³⁵U fission neutrons are β-delayed, emitted after precursor half-lives of about 0.2–56 s, and they stretch reactor kinetics to controllable timescales. β decay of fission products also supplies about 6–7% of full power as decay heat just after shutdown, and the reactor antineutrino flux.

name: Neutron moderation and resonance absorption
summary: Reactor physics is applied low-energy neutron reaction theory. Elastic scattering moderates neutrons (mean lethargy gain ξ, equal to 1 for hydrogen), and Breit–Wigner resonances of ²³⁸U set the resonance-escape probability p. Doppler broadening of those resonances gives the prompt negative fuel-temperature coefficient.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

name: Nuclear PDFs as the baseline for jet quenching
summary: Hard probes in A–A collisions are computed with collinear factorization. Nuclear PDFs (shadowing, antishadowing, the EMC effect), fixed by p–A and e–A data, remove initial-state effects so that R_AA isolates final-state energy loss in the QGP.
sources: PHENIX Collaboration (2005). "Formation of dense partonic matter in relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions at RHIC: Experimental evaluation by the PHENIX Collaboration". *Nucl. Phys. A* 757, 184. [arXiv:nucl-ex/0410003](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-ex/0410003)

name: Gluon saturation sets hydrodynamic initial conditions
summary: The color-glass-condensate picture of high-energy nuclei, with a saturation scale Q_s² ∝ A^{1/3}, underlies initial-state models such as IP-Glasma. Their event-by-event geometric fluctuations become the flow harmonics v_n. The EIC will measure nuclear gluon densities and Q_s directly in e–A collisions.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: g_A links neutron decay to nucleon structure
summary: g_A = G_A(0) ≈ 1.27 is the nucleon axial form factor at zero momentum transfer. It is measured in neutron-decay asymmetries and computed in lattice QCD. The neutron lifetime depends on g_A and on V_ud, which superallowed 0⁺→0⁺ decays fix independently.
sources: Hardy & Towner (2020). "Superallowed 0+→0+ nuclear β decays: 2020 critical survey, with implications for Vud and CKM unitarity". *Phys. Rev. C* 102, 045501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501)

name: EMC effect tracks short-range NN correlations
summary: The EMC effect is the depletion of nuclear valence-quark distributions at 0.3<x<0.7. Its slope scales linearly across nuclei with the density of short-range-correlated pairs (a_2, from x>1 scattering). Those pairs are mostly np because of the tensor force, which suggests that high-momentum nucleons are the ones modified.
breaks: A correlation, not a proven cause: mean-field modification models also fit the data.

name: QCD crossover vs inhomogeneous Big Bang nucleosynthesis
summary: A first-order cosmological QCD transition (~10 μs after the Big Bang) could have left baryon-density inhomogeneities with neutron–proton segregation, and in the 1980s this motivated inhomogeneous BBN. Lattice QCD shows a crossover at T≈155 MeV for small μ_B, and standard homogeneous BBN with the CMB baryon density fits D and ⁴He, so the scenario has lost its motivation.
map: T_c\approx155\,{\rm MeV}\ (t\sim10\,\mu{\rm s})\ \gg\ T_{\rm BBN}\approx0.07\,{\rm MeV}
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Heavy-ion flow and mergers constrain dense matter
summary: Directed and elliptic flow in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions constrains the pressure of symmetric nuclear matter at about 2–4.5 n_0. Combined with chiral EFT and astrophysical data, these flow results tighten the neutron-star EOS. Neutron-star mergers reach similar densities and tens-of-MeV temperatures and are modelled with the same relativistic (viscous) hydrodynamics.
breaks: Collisions probe near-symmetric, hot, transient matter. Neutron stars are cold and very isospin-asymmetric, so the link needs the symmetry energy.

name: NN phase shifts and the effective-range expansion
summary: Chiral NN potentials are fitted to partial-wave NN scattering phase shifts. The unnaturally large ¹S₀ scattering length (a_np ≈ −23.7 fm) shapes the EFT power counting and gives few-nucleon systems the same low-energy universality seen in cold atoms.
sources: Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)
Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)

name: Trace anomaly: nucleon mass and QGP ε−3P
summary: One operator, the QCD energy-momentum trace including the gluon anomaly, gives both the nucleon mass (an EIC target through threshold J/ψ production) and the QGP interaction measure (ε−3P)/T⁴. Lattice QCD finds the interaction measure peaks just above T_c.
breaks: The proton-mass decomposition is scheme-dependent, and how threshold J/ψ data relate to the gluon anomaly term is disputed.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: Hoyle state: triple-alpha to ab initio
summary: In 1953 Hoyle predicted the 7.65 MeV 0⁺ state of ¹²C because carbon could not be made in stars without a resonant triple-α reaction. Its α-cluster structure is a demanding test that nuclear lattice EFT has reproduced, and its energy and radiative width set the stellar carbon/oxygen yield.
map: E_{\rm Hoyle}-3m_\alpha c^2\approx0.38\,{\rm MeV};\quad r_{3\alpha}\propto\Gamma_{\rm rad}\,T^{-3}e^{-Q/kT}
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Th/U cosmochronometry of r-process stars
summary: The long-lived r-process actinides ²³²Th (14.0 Gyr) and ²³⁸U (4.47 Gyr) decay through α chains. Their abundances, relative to each other and to stable r-process elements, date old metal-poor stars, and live ²⁴⁴Pu and ⁶⁰Fe in deep-sea crusts time recent nearby nucleosynthesis.

name: Radiative energy loss: QED in matter vs QCD in plasma
summary: Medium-induced gluon bremsstrahlung (BDMPS-Z) is the QCD counterpart of radiative energy loss in matter, and it inherits the LPM coherence suppression first found in QED showers. Collisional loss plays the role of Bethe–Bloch ionization.
breaks: Radiated gluons carry color and rescatter, so ΔE grows as L² instead of L. The medium is an expanding hot plasma rather than a cold absorber, so q̂ depends on temperature and time instead of being a material constant.

name: Imaging nuclear deformation with collective flow
summary: In ultracentral collisions of deformed nuclei (²³⁸U, ¹²⁹Xe) and isobars (⁹⁶Ru/⁹⁶Zr), v₂ grows with the ground-state quadrupole deformation β₂² and is sensitive to triaxiality γ and neutron skins. Hydrodynamic flow thus becomes a snapshot probe of low-energy collective structure.

name: Nuclear pairing and neutron-star superfluidity
summary: The BCS pairing that causes odd–even mass staggering and reduced rotational moments of inertia in nuclei also makes neutron-star matter superfluid: ¹S₀ neutrons in the inner crust and ³P₂ neutrons in the core. The gaps are of order MeV, and the superfluid controls glitches, the specific heat and neutrino cooling.
breaks: Finite nuclei are smaller than the coherence length, so pairing there is a mesoscopic, fluctuating condensate. Whether Cas A's cooling shows ³P₂ pairing onset is contested.

name: Gamma-ray arrays map nuclear level schemes
summary: Compton-suppressed HPGe arrays (Gammasphere, and now AGATA and GRETA with γ-ray tracking), with ≈2 keV resolution at 1.33 MeV, resolve high-spin cascades. That resolution is what revealed rotational and superdeformed bands, band crossings and shell evolution, and the arrays are the workhorse instruments of in-beam structure studies.
